intent: Example Spring Boot app, example chart and a kind end-to-end test on JDK 21 and 25
Example app, example chart, kind end-to-end test and the extracted-JAR detection fix

title: recognise an extracted Spring Boot JAR as an ordinary executable JAR
why: The JAR written by -Djarmode=tools extract keeps Spring-Boot-Version but gets the application's Main-Class and a Class-Path to lib/. Treating the version attribute alone as a fat JAR made train refuse it, run tell users to extract an already extracted JAR, and fetch try to extract it again. A fat JAR keeps its dependencies in BOOT-INF, so it never has a Class-Path.
alternative: Require Start-Class or Spring-Boot-Classes — rejected: breaks fat JARs whose manifests carry only the version, and the existing fixtures

title: run the end-to-end test against a registry on the kind network, addressed by IP
why: The archive store must be reachable from pods without cluster DNS or containerd registry configuration; a registry container on the kind network is reachable by its address, and images are loaded into the node with kind load.
alternative: A registry configured through containerd patches and DNS names — rejected: more moving parts than the test needs

title: assert cache use through the JVM's own class-load log, and fallback through a JVM option changed only in the Deployment
why: Startup time is noisy on a shared machine; the application class's load source ('shared objects file' versus the JAR) is exact. A relevant option such as -Xmx added only to the Deployment's command leaves fetch's fingerprint matching but makes run reject the archive, which is the realistic way a team breaks it.

name: example app
role: A Spring Boot 3.5 web app extracted at image build time, used by the example chart and the kind test
conditions: One image per JDK (--build-arg JDK); compiled for 21

name: example-app chart
role: A workload chart using mnemo-warmup as an aliased dependency and its pod-template helpers
conditions: warmup.app.jvmArgs feeds the trainer, fetch and the Deployment's command so they agree; javaOptions is for options that do not matter to an archive

subject: dependency:go-offline
why: It failed after almost four minutes for the Spring Boot plugin; a BuildKit cache mount on ~/.m2 caches just as well

subject: Extracted Spring Boot manifest
why: Spring-Boot-Version survives extraction, so the version attribute cannot identify a fat JAR

subject: Real Spring Boot was never exercised before
why: Earlier tests used tiny plain JARs, which hid the detection problem

intent: Address review: framework identity vs extraction, isolated chart builds, strict class-load checks

title: separate a JAR's framework identity from whether it needs extraction
why: My first fix made an extracted Spring Boot JAR an EXECUTABLE_JAR, which broke build and bench in the default spring-refresh mode (it requires a Spring Boot app) and was hidden because train had its own workaround. Kind.SPRING_BOOT again means the framework; needsExtraction(jar) says whether a fat JAR must be extracted first, and prepare() returns the app unchanged with its real kind when it need not be.
alternative: Keep two kinds and special-case spring-refresh — rejected: spreads the distinction over every exit mode

title: build chart dependencies in a throw-away copy and make class-load checks fail when they cannot look
why: helm dependency build writes charts/ and Chart.lock beside a chart and the scripts used to delete them, destroying a developer's vendored dependencies. A negative check that passes on an empty or failed result proves nothing, so the checks now require the exec to succeed and positively match the expected source.
alternative: Track and restore only what the run created — rejected: a copy cannot lose anything

subject: Regression tests must be seen to fail
why: The new build/bench tests were run against the previous commit in a separate worktree and fail with the reviewer's exact error, so they do catch the regression

subject: An absent assertion looks like a pass
why: A not-contains check on a failed command output passes; require success and a positive match

intent: Release prep: version string, e2e rollout race, README status

title: select only live, settled pods in the end-to-end test after a rollout
why: rollout status returns when the new replicas are ready, while the old pods can stay in phase Running for a few seconds as they terminate. On the slower CI runner the test inspected an old pod (fetch log: no archive; exec: pod already Failed). The test now ignores pods with a deletionTimestamp, waits until exactly the expected number of ready pods remain, and dumps logs on any failure.
alternative: Sleep a fixed time after the rollout — rejected: still a guess on a slower runner

title: report the version from the jar manifest instead of a hard-coded string
why: --version printed mnemo-warmup 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT in every build including v0.1.0. The shaded jar's manifest now carries Implementation-Version from the pom, which versions:set stamps on a release, and a build outside a jar says dev.
alternative: Keep editing a string at release time — rejected: it was forgotten once already

title: call the project alpha, not pre-alpha, and say what is not proven
why: The whole chain is verified on a real cluster with two JDKs and both cache types, but only on arm64, with one small application, an unpublished chart and unstable options and formats; the status paragraph now says both halves instead of relying on a badge.
alternative: Beta — rejected: too little coverage and interfaces still free to change

subject: rollout status is not 'old pods are gone'
why: It completes once the new replicas are ready; terminating old pods still match a label selector and report phase Running, so selectors must exclude pods with a deletionTimestamp

subject: zsh path variable
why: In zsh the variable name path is tied to PATH, so a loop over a variable called path wipes the search path

intent: Chart publishing: classic Helm repo, version = release

title: publish the chart as a classic Helm repository like warden, with the chart version equal to the release version
why: The owner's Artifact Hub account already works with this pattern, and Artifact Hub's tracker times out on release assets, so a Pages mirror serves the packages. Stamping the release number into the chart (version, appVersion, default tools image tag) stops it drifting from the app it deploys, as 0.1.0 against 0.2.0 just did; a test fails if the repository's numbers disagree.
alternative: Independent chart version — rejected: it had already drifted

subject: Pages was never enabled
why: The coverage badge image works through raw.githubusercontent.com, but the site and any Helm repository on gh-pages need Pages enabled; the site root returned 404

subject: Coverage deploy deletes other gh-pages files
why: JamesIves deploy cleans the branch by default, so index.yaml, charts/ and artifacthub-repo.yml need clean-exclude

subject: Chart README links
why: The README is bundled into the package and shown on Artifact Hub, where relative links do not resolve
